lines: MASTER SUPPLY AGREEMENT (fictional sample document)
Between Northwind Supply Ltd ('Buyer') and Harbor Fabrication Co. ('Supplier').
Dated 14 November 2025.
7. Delivery
7.1 The Supplier shall deliver Goods to the address stated in the Purchase Order.
7.2 Delivery dates stated in a Purchase Order are binding. Time is of the essence
only where the Purchase Order expressly says so.
7.3 The Supplier shall notify the Buyer promptly of any expected delay.
9. Rejection
9.1 The Buyer may reject non-conforming Goods by written notice within 5 business days of delivery.
9.2 Rejected Goods are held at the Supplier's risk pending collection.
12. Governing law: the law of Exampleshire (a fictional jurisdiction).

name: Draft brief for Northwind
description: Northwind's draft submission. v1 contains the planted sample errors; v2 is the revised argument.

versions.preview: 8 pages. Asserts delivery on 3 March (p. 4 l. 12). Quotes Example Co. v. Sample Corp. (p. 6 l. 3).
versions.seededDefect: Planted sample errors: (1) p. 4 l. 12 states delivery on 3 March 2026, contradicted by the signed receipt (10 March); (2) p. 6 l. 3 misquotes the fictional authority Example Co. v. Sample Corp. All documents and authorities are fictional.

lines: III. FACTS
Harbor delivered the goods on 3 March 2026, two days after the agreed date,
and the delivery included units with coating defects.
Northwind rejected the delivery by written notice on 12 March 2026.
IV. ARGUMENT
A. Time was of the essence
As held in Example Co. v. Sample Corp. (fictional authority), 'time is of the essence in all commercial deliveries'.
PO-4471 stated a delivery date of 1 March 2026 and expressly made time of the essence.
B. Rejection was timely
Under MSA clause 9.1 the Buyer may reject within five business days of delivery.
Northwind's notice of 12 March was within that window.

versions.preview: 8 pages. States delivery on 10 March (p. 4 l. 12), corrects the quotation (p. 6 l. 3) and adds a response to the waiver point (p. 7).
versions.notes: Revised argument approved by Jonathan Reyes (apr-L-rec-001, apr-L-rec-002).

lines: III. FACTS
Harbor delivered the goods on 10 March 2026, nine days after the agreed date,
and the receipt records coating defects on 12 of the 400 units.
Northwind rejected the delivery by written notice on 12 March 2026, two business days later.
IV. ARGUMENT
A. Time was of the essence
As held in Example Co. v. Sample Corp. (fictional authority), 'time is of the essence only where the contract expressly so provides'.
PO-4471 expressly so provides, and MSA clause 7.2 gives that wording effect.
B. Rejection was timely and not waived
Under MSA clause 9.1 the Buyer may reject within five business days of delivery; the notice of 12 March was within that window.
The receipt itself recorded the defects, so no unreserved acceptance occurred (contrast Placeholder Industries v. Specimen Logistics, fictional authority).

name: Example Co. v. Sample Corp. (fictional authority)
description: Sample authority, not a real case. Stands for: time is of the essence only where the contract expressly so provides.

authority.name: Example Co. v. Sample Corp. (fictional authority)
authority.fictionalLabel: Sample authority, not a real case
authority.proposition: Time is of the essence only where the contract expressly so provides; a stated date alone does not make it so.

lines: Example Co. v. Sample Corp. (fictional authority) [2019] (sample)
Sample authority, not a real case.
Held: time is of the essence only where the contract expressly so provides.
A stated delivery date, without more, does not make time of the essence.

name: Placeholder Industries v. Specimen Logistics (fictional authority)
description: Sample authority, not a real case. Contrary: unreserved acceptance of a late delivery may waive the right to reject.

versions.preview: Fictional first-instance decision, 2021 (sample). Surfaced by the contrary-authority search.
